 The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi
 Writ Petition No.36521 of 2022
Order:

{Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy} Sri Mohd. Gouse Baba, the detenu, has filed this Habeas Corpus Petition challenging the detention order passed by the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police & Additional District Magistrate, Karimnagar, in C.No.119/PDC/KNR/2022, dated 26.05.2022, whereby, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2)
of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders,
Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (in short, 'the PD Act'), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1446, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, dated 14.07.2022,
AAR,J & JS,J passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration Department,
Government of Telangana.
2. Heard Sri Pasham Trivikram Reddy, the learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Mujib Kumar, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents and perused the record.
3.

The case of the petitioner is that basing on two crimes viz., Crime Nos.68/2022 and 72/2022 of LMD Colony Police Station, Karimnagar Police Commissionerate, registered for the offence under Section 379 I.P.C., the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned detention order dated 26.05.2022.

entities.text: LMD Colony Police Station, Karimnagar Police Commissionerate
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
According to respondent No.2, the detenu is a 'goonda', as he has been indulging in a series of offences such as theft and automobile thefts in the limits of Karimangar Police Commissionerate,
thereby creating large scale fear and panic among the people and Automobile Operators, thus adversely affecting the maintenance of public order.

Subsequently, the impugned detention order was confirmed by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.1446 dated 14.07.2021.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the impugned detention order has been passed in a mechanical manner AAR,J & JS,J and without application of mind.
Already criminal law was set into motion against the detenu.

In the two crimes relied upon by the detaining authority,
statutory bail was granted to the detenu on 16.05.2022.

But, even before the detenu was released from the jail, the impugned detention order was passed on the apprehension that there is imminent Md Gouse Baba vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100131414/
1 possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities again, which is unjustified..

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The alleged crimes do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the word "law and order".
Since the offence alleged is under the Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted under the penal code.
Thus, there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu.
Hence, the impugned orders tantamount to colourable exercise of power.

The impugned orders are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to allow the Writ Petition, as prayed for.
5.
On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the detenu is a 'goonda'.

He has been indulging in a series of offences such as theft and automobile thefts and thereby AAR,J & JS,J creating large scale fear and panic among the public and Automobile Operators, and his activities are adversely affecting the public order, apart from disturbing peace, tranquility and social harmony in the society and as such, it necessitated the respondent No.2 to pass the impugned detention order against the detenu.

Since the detenu was granted statutory bail in the two crimes relied upon by the detaining authority, the apprehension of the detaining authority that after release of the detenu on bail, there is every possibility of his again indulging in similar offences, which would be detrimental to public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an appropriate order of detention, is not misconceived.
The series of crimes allegedly committed by the detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the general public and automobile operators.
The unlawful activities of the detenu have created sufficient panic in the minds of the general public.

Therefore,
the detaining authority was legally justified in passing the impugned detention order.

Further, the Advisory Board rendered its opinion that there was sufficient cause for detention of the detenu and on considering the same along with the entire material, the Government confirmed the impugned detention order AAR,J & JS,J vide G.O.Rt.No.1446 dated 14.07.2022.
All the mandatory requirements were strictly followed by the detaining authority while passing the impugned detention order.
The impugned orders are legally sustainable and ultimately, prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.

6. In view of the submissions made by both the sides, the point that arises for determination in this Writ Petition is:
"Whether the impugned detention order vide C.No.119/PDC/KNR/2022, dated 26.05.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1446, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order))
Department, dated 14.07.2022, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, Government of Telangana, are liable to be set aside?"

POINT:
7.
In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order".

The offences committed against a particular individual fall within the ambit of "law and order" and when the public at large is adversely affected by the Md Gouse Baba vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100131414/
2 criminal activities of a AAR,J & JS,J person, such activities of that person are said to disturb the public order.

entities.text: Md Gouse Baba vs The State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, individual cases can be dealt with by the criminal justice system.

Therefore,
there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws against an individual.
Hence, according to the Hon'ble Apex Court, the detaining authority should be wary of invoking the immense power under the Act.
8. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem.

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'.
The distinction has to be borne in mind in view of what has been stated in the grounds of detention.

9. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a AIR 1966 SC 740 (1972) 3 SCC 831 AAR,J &
JS,J disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society.

sentences.text: As seen from the material placed on record, the two crimes relied upon by the detaining authority for preventively detaining the detenu relate to theft and automobile thefts.
The detenu was granted statutory bail in the said two crimes relied upon by the AAR,J & JS,J detaining authority.
As seen from the counter affidavit filed by the respondent No.2, the two crimes relied upon by the detaining authority are pending for trial before the Courts concerned.

Under these circumstances, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every possibility of the detenu again indulging in criminal activities which are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an appropriate order of detention, is highly misplaced.
Moreover, criminal law was already set into motion against the detenu.

Since the detenu has allegedly committed the offence punishable under the Indian Penal Code, the said crime can be effectively dealt with under the provisions of the Penal code and there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law.

Thus, the offence allegedly committed by the detenu in the two crimes relied upon by the detaining authority does not fall within the ambit of the words "public order" or "disturbance of public order".
Instead, they fall within the scope of the words "law and order".
Hence, there was no need for the detaining authority to pass the impugned detention order.
The detaining authority cannot be AAR,J & JS,J permitted to subvert, supplant or substitute the punitive law of land, by ready resort to preventive detention.
12. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned orders are legally unsustainable and are liable to be set aside.
13. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide C.No.119/PDC/KNR/2022, dated 26.05.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1446 dated 14.07.2022, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely, Md. Gouse Baba S/o.Ashraf, at liberty forthwith,
in case he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition
shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
